question:
Choose the idiom / phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

They are **working very hard in less time** to make the presentation on time.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Working against the clock"** means working very hard and fast in order to complete a task within a limited time. (समय के खिलाफ काम करना)

 
 
• **Example: **We are **working against the clock** to finish the project by the deadline.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Scapegoat** (बलि का बकरा): A person who is blamed for the wrongdoings, mistakes, or faults of others.

 
 
• **Example:** The manager became the scapegoat for the team's failure.
 
 
 
• **Off on the wrong foot** (गलत शुरुआत करना): To make a bad start at something, especially a relationship or a task.
 
 
• **Example:** Our new project got off on the wrong foot due to some initial misunderstandings.
 
 
 
• **Til the cows come home** (बहुत लम्बे समय तक): For a very long time, or forever.
 
 
• **Example:** We could argue about this until the cows come home and still not reach an agreement.
